character: Mel: everyday Kiwi woman, late 30s, the straight-talking one in the group chat who actually reads the small print. Talking for Q-S-me, owning up with a half-smile: we started in Auckland, here's exactly what you get everywhere else. General NZ accent, never a caricature. Dry, warm, under-played, like explaining it to a mate over a Saturday coffee. Facts flat and plain; the two jokes ('They knew.' and 'We know.') thrown away, never pushed.
voice: Mel casting in projects/2026-10-02-qsme-voice-casting: Jenna 7R9vnLAE0ZSpY0xWp0mv or Ellie BujbDaM2eT58IpdbIc8J (tools/voices.json qsme-nz). Same voice as the rest of the NZ series.
casting_line: Straight answer for everyone outside Auckland. Yeah. We started in Auckland. We know.

pronunciation.QSME: Q-S-me (Cue Ess Me, kyoo-ess-mee), never 'kiss me', never four letters
pronunciation.qsme.co.nz: Q-S-me dot co dot en zed
pronunciation.Christchurch: KRAIS-church, two quick syllables, the t disappears
pronunciation.never said: Octagon, Hereford, Anglesea, LINZ, PIM (on screen only)

continuous_read_v2:
Straight answer for everyone outside Auckland.

Fair test: we typed in each council's own address.

Anywhere in the country: the boundary… land area, legal description and council.

Services and hazards? Not here yet. It says so.

We told the council it's in Dunedin City. They knew.

Four councils add the planning zone.
Christchurch: Commercial Zone.
Hamilton: Central City Zone.
Wellington City: the zone too. Hazards? Not yet.

And Auckland gets the whole card.
The zone, then pipes, power, flood and hazard checks.
That's another video: The back corner.

So. Everywhere: the basics. Three more councils: plus the zone. Auckland: the lot.

Wherever you are, it's not a LIM.
Still order the LIM. Check the title. Ask council or a planner.

Yeah. We started in Auckland. We know. Card says so.

Search your address. Sign up at Q-S-me dot co dot en zed.

post_processing: v2 is the default: continuous read first as the pitch/accent reference, then each line as its own request with previous_text/next_text (make_vo.py does this). vo05 is one request; vo16-vo18 may be one request cut in the edit so 'We know.' starts on the slam at 69.0.
Fit to time by trimming head/tail silence and closing gaps over room tone; never time-stretch more than about 4%. If a take runs past max_s, use another take.
Room tone bed (60-90 s of a quiet kitchen on the same phone) under the whole VO at -48 to -45 dBFS, most important 66.8-70.0 where the music drops out.
Phone voice-memo EQ: HPF about 90 Hz, -2 to -3 dB shelf from 10 kHz, 1-2 dB dip at 6-8 kHz, light de-ess; 2:1-3:1 compression, 2-4 dB GR; no reverb.
Music about 14 dB under speech; ducks hard 21.3-23.0; thins 59.0-66.8; out 66.8-70.0; re-enters under vo18; resolves 75.9.
